title: Operational GovOps can block the rebate surplus distribution and must escalate unresolved disputes to Core GovOps
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3 splits calculation from execution: "Operational GovOps reviews Skybase's calculation of the rebate before executing a return of surplus to token holders. In the event of any issues, Operational GovOps cannot execute the distribution."

The prohibition is phrased as an incapacity, not a discretion — where issues exist, GovOps *cannot* proceed. There is no override available to Skybase, and no ability for GovOps to execute a corrected figure of its own; the only paths are agreement or escalation.

The dispute procedure is then fully specified: GovOps "must post an explanation on the Sky Forum under the 'Skybase Prime' category and work with Skybase to resolve the disagreement," and "if Operational GovOps and Skybase cannot resolve the disagreement, it must be escalated to Core GovOps."

Three properties make this a strong control. The blocking party is not the calculating party, so self-reported figures cannot self-execute. Disagreement is forced into public view before resolution, so a stalemate is visible to token holders rather than silent. And the terminal arbiter sits *above* the Agent — Core GovOps — so a deadlock cannot be resolved by whoever has more leverage inside Skybase.

The cost is a live liveness risk: token holders' surplus can be withheld indefinitely while a dispute climbs the escalation ladder, and nothing in the provision bounds how long that may take.
description: Skybase computes the rebate but cannot execute the return to token holders; a GovOps objection requires a public Forum explanation and, if unresolved, escalation outside the Agent entirely.
